page: Vultr vx1-g-8c-32g is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is limited to a 1 GB network-attached volume, and there are no onboard GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-threaded performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in single-core stress-ng CPU tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Geekbench text processing also ranks in the top tier. Conversely, multi-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench falls into the average category. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached reads and writes consistently register in the middle tier.

For LLM inference, the server demonstrates strong text generation speed with a small 135M model, but drops to a weak tier for prompt processing on a medium 7B model. The lack of local NVMe storage and reliance on a 1 GB network volume limits its utility for storage-heavy applications. This profile is suitable for general-purpose workloads, text processing pipelines, and single-threaded execution tasks that benefit from dedicated AMD EPYC cores without requiring high local disk throughput.
description: The Vultr vx1-g-8c-32g is a general-purpose server instance from the VX1 Cloud Compute family, equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical AMD EPYC cores and 32.0 GB of RAM. Operating at 2.0 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server features a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and relies on a 1 GB network storage volume with no local GPU resources. Performance benchmarks show top-tier capabilities in single-threaded operations, including stress-ng single-core CPU tests, gzip compression, and text processing. However, multi-core execution, memory bandwidth, and database operations align with average mid-tier performance. LLM inference is efficient for small models but degrades on larger workloads. This resource profile is suitable for general-purpose computing, text processing, and single-threaded applications that do not require high-capacity local storage.
